relay.pairing.screen_title.note: Header of the full-screen pairing route (#/pair). Imperative, short.

relay.pairing.back.note: aria-label of the header back arrow on the pairing screen.

relay.pairing.title.note: First thing a person sees when they choose to pair the phone with their computer. Names the benefit, not the mechanism.

relay.pairing.title_for_action.role: pairing sheet title opened from an approval
relay.pairing.title_for_action.note: Sheet title when the person tapped Approve (or a run-without-asking choice) on a phone that is not paired yet. The sheet opens in place; after pairing they return to the same request. 'Approve' is the same verb as the approval card's button.

relay.pairing.intro.body.note: Explains the grant (this phone gains the power to approve actions), that the computer confirms with its own (computer login) password, not a Radient password, and the scope of the grant: computers that later join this computer's network will trust the phone too (consent disclosure, design A2/D14).

relay.pairing.intro.not_now.note: Dismisses the pairing sheet without doing anything.

relay.pairing.checking.note: Shown while the phone asks the computer whether it can pair phones.

relay.pairing.unavailable.body.note: The computer cannot approve phones yet. 'Local Operator → Settings → Phone access' is the navigation path in the desktop app: translate 'Settings' and 'Phone access' exactly as the desktop app's settings labels in this locale (see the glossary); keep the arrows. Never mention terminals or commands here.

relay.pairing.unavailable.waiting.note: Shown under unavailable.body: the phone re-checks every few seconds and files the request by itself once phone approvals are on. 'they' = phone approvals.

relay.pairing.unsupported.body.note: The computer runs a version without terminal-free pairing.

relay.pairing.filing.note: Shown while the phone files its pairing request.

relay.pairing.waiting.title.note: The request is waiting on the computer: the person should open the desktop app (or terminal app) there, where a pairing request appears.

relay.pairing.waiting.confirm_body.note: Confirm mode: the computer shows the same six digits; the person compares them and approves on the computer. The code is shown above this line.

relay.pairing.waiting.code_body.note: Code mode: the computer asks the person to type the six digits shown above this line.

relay.pairing.waiting.password.note: After approving, the computer asks for its own login password (or Touch ID) to confirm. 'its own' distinguishes it from a Radient account password.

relay.pairing.waiting.expires.note: {countdown} is minutes:seconds, e.g. 4:59. Keep it as one token.

relay.pairing.waiting.not_seen.note: Appears after about a minute without an answer.

relay.pairing.waiting.cancel.note: Withdraws this phone's pending pairing request.

relay.pairing.code.aria.role: accessible label of the six-digit code
relay.pairing.code.aria.note: Screen readers read {digits} digit by digit (the digits separated by spaces, e.g. '4 8 2 9 1 3').

relay.pairing.signing.note: The person approved on the computer and the computer's password prompt is open. 'password' is the computer's login password.

relay.pairing.failed_retryable.note: The computer's password prompt was dismissed; the request is still open and can be approved again on the computer.

relay.pairing.strikes_exhausted.note: The person typed the wrong code on the COMPUTER three times; the pairing request is closed. 'Pair again' is the button below.

relay.pairing.denied.note: Someone chose Deny on the computer for the PAIRING. Must name pairing, not 'the request': the sheet sits over an action card whose own request is still pending.

relay.pairing.expired.note: The pairing window closed without an answer. Name pairing, not 'the request' (the action is still pending).

relay.pairing.withdrawn.note: This phone's pairing request was withdrawn (by this phone's Cancel). Name pairing, not 'the request'.

relay.pairing.withdraw_in_progress.note: Cancel was tapped too late: the computer is mid-confirmation, so the phone can't withdraw.

relay.pairing.withdraw_failed.note: The withdraw call failed for a transport reason.

relay.pairing.paired.not_ready.note: Paired, but the computer has not finished setting up phone approvals, so it cannot yet verify this phone's approvals. Same navigation path wording as unavailable.body.

relay.pairing.paired.home_screen.note: Browsers may clear storage of sites not added to the Home Screen; adding it keeps the pairing key. Use the platform's usual name for 'Add to Home Screen' in this locale.

relay.pairing.return.approve.note: Shown when pairing started from an approval: the original request is still waiting and needs a fresh tap. 'Approve' is the card's button label; the phone never approves on its own.

relay.pairing.return.choose.note: Shown when pairing started from the approval-mode sheet (run without asking): the choice needs a fresh tap.

relay.pairing.return.gone.note: The request the person wanted to approve is gone (handled on another device, or it timed out). Pairing still succeeded.

relay.pairing.return.back.note: Closes the sheet and returns to the request still waiting.

relay.pairing.busy.same_key.note: An earlier request from this same phone is still open on the computer.

relay.pairing.busy.resume.note: Resumes waiting on the earlier request.

relay.pairing.busy.cancel_earlier.note: Withdraws the earlier request so a new one can be filed.

relay.pairing.busy.other.note: A different phone's request is open on the computer; only one can be open at a time. Tells the person to deny it on the computer if it isn't theirs (safety).

relay.pairing.rate_limited_later.note: Same refusal as relay.pairing.rate_limited, shown when the computer did not say how long to wait, so no countdown is shown. 'Try again' button sits below.

relay.pairing.revoked.note: The computer removed (revoked) this phone. The phone has discarded its old key; pairing again files a fresh request that needs a new approval on the computer.

relay.pairing.key_lost.note: The browser evicted the phone's private key; the old pairing can no longer sign.

relay.pairing.refused_signature.note: The computer rejected this phone's signed approval (for example the phone was removed or its pairing expired).

relay.pairing.error.no_crypto.note: The browser lacks the secure key storage pairing needs.

relay.pairing.terminal.header.note: Collapsed section with the terminal-based alternatives. The only place on these screens where commands appear.

relay.pairing.terminal.turn_on_approving.note: {command} is a literal slash command (e.g. /mobile approvals on) and stays untranslated.

relay.pairing.terminal.code_intro.note: {command} is a literal shell command and stays untranslated.

relay.pairing.terminal.name_label.note: Label of the device-name input; the computer shows this name with the request.

relay.pairing.terminal.waiting.note: {name} is the phone name the person typed.

relay.pairing.terminal.no_answer.note: Waited ten minutes without an approval.

relay.pairing.busy.maybe_this_phone.note: Shown under busy.other. On iPhones, Safari and the Home Screen web app keep separate storage, so the same phone pairing from both looks like a second phone to the computer. Hedged ('might'): the phone cannot tell for sure.

relay.pairing.error.refused.note: The computer answered but refused to start pairing (an unexpected refusal, often an older or mismatched Local Operator). Distinct from error.network: the connection works, so do not mention it.

relay.pairing.error.support_code.note: Small text under an error. {code} is a technical identifier such as approval_invalid or 500; keep it untranslated.

relay.pairing.rate_limited_over.note: Spoken (polite live region) when the rate-limit wait ends and Try again unlocks.
